title: Near-term decommit protocol & pricing sensitivity — Q4 2026
content:
Executive summary:

This note defines a short-horizon decommit protocol for reserved GPU capacity, ties it to a pricing-sensitivity analysis across four price points, and models headcount and budget impacts across three operational scenarios. Goal: provide the Finance + Ops leadership a concrete runbook to reduce committed spend quickly if realized token demand falls below forecast while minimizing SLA risk for prioritized customers.

Context and motivation:
- Q3–Q4 2026 usage growth slowed vs. plan; we have ~38% of reserved GPU capacity under soft-utilization (avg utilization < 30% across hour windows).
- Reserved commitments are lumpy and front-loaded; early decommit triggers can materially reduce monthly committed spend but require careful headcount & SLA gating.
- Leadership requested a protocol that can be executed within a 2–6 week window and a pricing-sensitivity matrix to estimate revenue/headcount tradeoffs across modest to large price moves.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Current committed GPU spend (monthly amortized) = $4.2M.
- On-demand unit cost per effective token = $0.000012 (infrastructure + infra margin).
- Hosted API markup baseline per-token = $0.000050 (current public price for standard generation route).
- Average tokens per request and route mix assumed stable for 8 weeks unless we roll pricing changes.
- Hiring lag: 8–12 weeks to fully onboard an infra-facing engineer; contractor surge can be 2–3 weeks to operational scale.
- SLA priority tiers: P0 (enterprise dedicated), P1 (high-value PLG), P2 (standard). Decommit must preserve capacity for all P0 routes.

Protocol design (short):
1) Soft-signal monitoring window (7 days): Identify candidate reservations with sustained utilization < 35% and no P0 pinned allocations.
2) Canary decommit (2 weeks): Decommit 15% of candidate reservations; run traffic routing policies that shift low-priority routes to on-demand and lower-cost model variants. Verify error/backpressure metrics.
3) Full decommit tranche (4–6 weeks): If SLA & error budgets stable and savings in line, decommit additional 35% of candidate pool.
4) Human-in-loop pause: Any customer-impact alert auto-stops further decommit and schedules immediate rollback.

Scenario modelling (high level):
- Scenarios model changes to price and decommit volumes and estimate net monthly cash flow effect and headcount adjustments needed to support on-demand fallback.

Scenario A — Base (no price change):
- Decommit tranche: 50% of candidate pool (net reduction in reserved spend: $700k/mo).
- Shift cost to on-demand for lower tiers: +$120k/mo variable infra.
- Headcount: +1 contractor infra ops (3 weeks) to manage reroutes; net HC delta = 0 FTEs; contractor cost = $25k/mo.
- Net monthly run-rate savings: $700k - $120k - $25k = $555k.

Scenario B — Price +10% across hosted API (moderate increase):
- Expected demand elasticity (token-weighted) = -0.08 (low elasticity for enterprise, medium for PLG).
- Demand change: -3.2% overall tokens => further opportunity to decommit additional 10% of candidate pool (incremental reserved spend reduction: $140k/mo).
- Revenue impact from price change: +$420k/mo (price * remaining tokens).
- On-demand bump: +$95k/mo (less traffic to on-demand due to overall demand decline).
- Headcount: 0 change.
- Net monthly delta vs base: +$140k (savings) +$420k (price) -$95k = +$465k -> total incremental benefit.

Scenario C — Price -15% (aggressive discount to capture PLG volume):
- Elasticity estimate = 0.3 (PLG elastic), net demand +8% tokens, bringing incremental traffic to on-demand in short-run before rerouting optimizations settle.
- Required decommit pause (can't decommit further as demand rises). Incremental reserved spend change = -$0.
- Revenue impact: -$1.05M/mo (assuming discount on hosted routes across volumes).
- On-demand cost increase: +$300k/mo.
- Headcount: +1 full-time on-call infra (to manage burst operationally) = $18k/mo fully loaded.
- Net monthly delta: -$1.368M -> significant negative impact. Not recommended without longer-term pipeline studies.

Scenario D — Rapid demand collapse (stress):
- Tokens fall 22% (customer churn +PLG slowdown). We execute accelerated decommit (70% of candidate pool) and move P1/P2 to deeper on-demand/low-cost variants.
- Immediate reserved spend reduction: $980k/mo.
- On-demand variable cost: +$220k/mo.
- Headcount: -2 hiring freezes (saves ~ $72k/mo) + reallocate 1 infra FTE to runbook execution (no incremental spend). Net monthly savings: $980k - $220k + $72k = $832k.

Headcount phasing table (text):
- Weeks 0–2: +1 contractor infra ops (to manage canary); hold hiring across finance/back office.
- Weeks 3–6: Decide tranche 2 — if proceed, freeze 1-2 non-critical hires in infra/product (saves ~$36k–$72k/mo).
- Weeks 6–12: If demand remains depressed, convert contractor to temporary headcount or reassign product hires; plan for 2–3 month hiring pause.

Budget sensitivity (representative numbers):
- Current committed monthly spend: $4,200,000
- Candidate pool identified for decommit: $1,400,000 (33% of committed)
- Decommit 50% of candidate pool => reserved spend reduction = $700,000
- On-demand conversion cost at current routing = $120,000
- Net P&L benefit = $580,000 (approx) before tax/overheads

Pricing sensitivity matrix (per-token):
- Baseline hosted price: $0.000050
- +10% => $0.000055 => revenue delta driven by inelastic enterprise and slightly elastic PLG. Elasticity mixture used for calc: enterprise 0.02, PLG 0.25, blended -0.08 overall.
- -15% => $0.0000425 => see Scenario C above.

Break-even analysis for decommit timeline:
- One tranche (15% canary): engineering ops costs (contractor provisioning and routing changes) ~ $45k total over 2 months. If tranche yields at least $90k/mo in savings after on-demand delta, ROI < 30 days.
- Full 50% candidate decommit: setup costs amortized < 45 days for $700k/mo reductions.

Risk matrix (short):
- Customer SLA hits: Mitigate by preserving P0 capacity, canary windows, and automated rollback. Residual risk: medium.
- Hidden long-term demand rebound: Risk of lost market share if we tighten capacity aggressively combined with price increases. Mitigate by staged decommit and short-term reversible commitments (spot + short-term rentals).
- Talent morale & hiring friction: Hiring freezes and contractor usage will impact recruiting; mitigate with clear communication and internal redeployment paths.

Recommended guardrails and runbook (operational):
- Hard guardrail: never decommit resources that are pinned to any P0 allocation.
- Monitoring: real-time dashboard with utilization, latency percentiles, error rates; automated alerts at 10%/30%/50% post-decommit thresholds.
- Communication: 72h notice to customer success + account owners ahead of tranche 2 if any route migration could affect billing windows.
- Finance triggers: decommit tranche 2 only if last 14 days utilization < 30% and month-over-month tokens delta <= -5%.

Decision items for execs:
- Approve the 2-stage protocol (canary 15% then tranche up to 50% of candidate pool) as primary path.
- Authorize up to $60k one-time ops contractor budget for the canary window.
- Direction on pricing: do not pursue >+10% cross-product price increases without a 6-week A/B test targeted at non-price-sensitive enterprise routes.

Action list (owners):
- Sofia Patel (Finance): finalize forecast model and publish shared workbook (Due: 2026-11-18).
- Evan Monroe (Infra Ops): prepare canary runbook and dashboard queries (Due: 2026-11-20).
- Priya Kaur (Customer Success): identify top-25 accounts that must be preserved and confirm pinned allocations (Due: 2026-11-22).
- Liam O'Neill (Product): create fallback low-cost model variants and routing policies (Due: 2026-11-26).

Appendix A — Methodology notes:
- Demand elasticity inputs: blended from cohort A/B experiments run Aug–Sep 2026 and external benchmarks for PLG vs enterprise price sensitivity.
- Cost model: on-demand cost derived from infra usage telemetry + GPU amortization schedule. All numbers are monthly run rate for near-term window.
- Headcount costs = loaded costs (comp + benefits + hiring overhead). Contractor costs are estimated market rates for experienced infra ops.

Appendix B — Quick sensitivity calculator (walkthrough):
1) Change decommit percentage on candidate pool.
2) Adjust expected token elasticity and reroute mix.
3) Calculator outputs: reserved spend delta, on-demand delta, headcount delta, net monthly P&L.

Notes / open questions:
- Do we want to combine this protocol with an explicit customer credit program to reduce immediate churn risk if we change pricing? (Priya to advise)
- If we accelerate decommit to >70% candidate pool, what are the legal/contractual implications for reserved capacity in selected regions? (Legal input needed)
